title: Squared discrepancy of an inner-product rectangle
statement:
Fix $n \in \bbn$ and equip the product $\mathrm{BoolInput}(n) \times \mathrm{BoolInput}(n)$ with its uniform probability measure. For any two sets $A, B \subseteq \mathrm{BoolInput}(n)$, the discrepancy of the mod-2 inner product $\mathrm{IP}_n$ over the combinatorial rectangle $A \times B$ satisfies
\[
  \bigl(\mathrm{disc}(\mathrm{IP}_n,\, A \times B)\bigr)^2 \;\le\; \frac{1}{2^n}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: A and B are subsets of the n-bit Boolean input type
the product space carries the (uniform) finite probability measure supplied as the ambient instance
the rectangle is the product set A × B
the function is the mod-2 inner product
caveat: The probability measure on the product space enters the discrepancy through an instance argument rather than an explicit hypothesis, so it is not literally written in the declaration; the bound $2^{-n}$ is exactly the value forced by the uniform measure (and fails for arbitrary measures), so the ambient measure is taken to be uniform.
